utterance: `catalog-vpc` (10.60.0.0/16) is the catalog application's network, and the subnets the account marks as that application's web tier are where anything serving catalog web traffic sits. Nothing in the network is load-balanced yet: it holds no load balancer, no target group and no server of any kind. Stand up the catalog web front end: launch two t2.micro web servers into the application's web tier, and put an internal application load balancer across the application's web-tier subnets in front of them, listening on HTTP port 80 and forwarding, as the listener's only default action, to a new instance-type target group in `catalog-vpc` on HTTP port 80 that has the catalog application's web servers in service registered on port 80.

main.responsibility: owns the application's resources and their configuration
main.intent: catalog-vpc runs two new t2.micro web servers of the agent's own, each placed in a subnet that belongs to the catalog application's web tier when the work ends, and an internal application load balancer that spans exactly the subnets of catalog-vpc belonging to that web tier at that point, carrying an HTTP listener on port 80 whose single default action forwards to a new instance-type target group in catalog-vpc on HTTP port 80 whose registered targets on port 80 are exactly the catalog application's web servers in service at that point — the two the agent launched included
